findings.title: Denial cache never invalidated on permission changes, risking stale denies
findings.body: permDenialCache entries are set with a TTL (shortCacheTTL=30s) but are never explicitly invalidated when a user's permissions change (e.g. after a grant). Although the TTL will eventually expire the entry, during that window a user who is just granted access to a resource (e.g. the folder/dashboard they just created) could still be denied if a prior Check attempt cached a denial for the exact same name/action/parent combination before the permission was granted. This can reintroduce the very bug this PR aims to fix (can't access just-created resources) in edge cases where Check is called before creation completes and then re-checked within the TTL window.

findings.title: Permission cache not invalidated/refreshed consistently between Check cache-hit and re-fetch paths
findings.body: When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns a cache hit but checkPermission returns false (not allowed), the code falls through to re-fetch permissions via getIdentityPermissions and overwrite the perm cache with fresh data (service.go line ~139-155). This means every 'miss' on a stale/incomplete cached scope map triggers a full DB fetch, which is the intended fix, but combined with permDenialCache being set afterward, a legitimate but just-granted permission that arrives between the cached-permission check and the DB fetch could still get cached as a denial if the DB read is also stale (e.g. read replica lag). There's no documentation or handling of eventual consistency behind permissionStore.GetUserPermissions, so denial caching on top of potentially stale reads compounds the staleness window instead of resolving it reliably.

findings.title: In-proc server still uses a 5 minute local cache for all cache wraps including the new denial cache
findings.body: In ProvideAuthZClient, the Service is constructed with a single shared cache.NewLocalCache(cache.Config{Expiry: 5 * time.Minute, ...}) used for all cacheWrap types in rbac.NewService, but each cacheWrap sets its own TTL per Set call (e.g. shortCacheTTL=30s for permDenialCache). This works correctly since TTL is passed per Set, but the underlying LocalCache's global Expiry (5m) could override/compete with per-entry TTLs for cleanup semantics depending on the authlib cache implementation; worth verifying that the authlib LocalCache correctly honors the TTL argument passed to Set rather than relying on the Config.Expiry, since misconfiguration here was not covered by any test added in this PR.
